title: Fn, FnMut, FnOnce
goal: run_twice calls its argument twice. Demand the closure trait that makes that legal — with the least machinery.
hints: FnOnce means exactly what it says — the second f() is using a spent closure.
FnMut works if you declare the parameter mut. Fn asks for less and needs no mut at all.
explanation: Calling twice rules out FnOnce (the first call consumes f; the second is E0382). FnMut works — calling through it needs `mut f`, one extra pledge of machinery. Fn is the calmest contract: shared-borrow calls, no mut anywhere, and since every Fn closure is also FnMut and FnOnce, demanding Fn costs your CALLERS nothing extra for a print-only closure. The hierarchy nests — ask for the weakest trait your usage allows, in both directions.
